name: Rimless Nano Aquarium
summary: The 3N and 5N are the small UNS tanks a lot of people start with. They are low-iron rimless boxes with mitred corners, sized for a desk or shelf, and the 5N in particular has become a standard nano size that plenty of lights and filters are built around.
highlights: Two sizes: 3N (about 11 L) and 5N (about 17 L)
5 mm low-iron glass with 45 degree mitred corners
Proportions suit a shrimp tank, betta tank or a small iwagumi
bestFor: A first planted nano, a shrimp colony or a desk scape where you want a clean glass box without a rim.
watchOut: Small water volumes swing fast in temperature and parameters, so dose and top up with care.

name: Rimless Cube Aquarium
summary: Equal sides on every face, from a tiny 16 cm cube up to a 60 cm cube that holds over 200 litres. Cubes pull the eye to the centre of the layout, so they work well for a single strong focal point or a row of matching tanks.
highlights: Eight sizes from 16C (about 4 L) to 60C (about 216 L)
Glass steps up from 5 mm to 10 mm on the bigger sizes
45 degree mitred corners on low-iron glass
Levelling mat included
bestFor: Betta and shrimp tanks, centre-focused layouts, or a gallery of small cubes side by side.
watchOut: Cubes are deep for their width, so the larger ones need a strong light to reach the substrate and long tools to reach the back.

name: Rimless Standard Aquarium
summary: The core UNS range, running from the 45U through the very popular 60U up to a 180 cm show tank. These are classic rectangular proportions for a full foreground to background layout, with glass thickness that scales properly as the tanks get bigger.
highlights: Ten sizes from 45U (about 35 L) to 180U (about 648 L)
60U (60 x 36 x 36 cm, about 78 L) is the go-to mid-size planted tank
Glass from 5 mm up to 15 mm on the largest models
P, U and M suffixes give different depth and height options at 90 and 120 cm
Matching UNS stands exist for most sizes
bestFor: Nature-style and Dutch layouts where you want room for a proper foreground, midground and background.
watchOut: From 75P upwards these are heavy tanks, so plan the stand and floor loading before you buy.

name: Rimless Shallow Aquarium
summary: Low-profile tanks that put the focus on rockwork, carpets and negative space. Light reaches the substrate easily and top-down viewing becomes part of the display.
highlights: Eleven sizes from 16S (about 2 L) up to 120S (about 259 L)
SS models at 90 and 120 cm are extra shallow (25 cm tall)
Low height means carpets need less light and are easy to reach
5 mm to 12 mm glass depending on size
bestFor: Iwagumi, carpet-heavy layouts and open-top scapes viewed from above as well as the front.
watchOut: Less water column means less room for tall stems and fewer fish, and evaporation shows quickly.

name: Rimless Tall Aquarium
summary: Taller versions of the familiar UNS footprints, built for vertical layouts. Extra height gives stem plants room to grow and lets branches or rock reach up and out of the water.
highlights: Eight sizes from 16T (about 6 L) to 60T (about 97 L)
Same footprints as the cube, nano and standard tanks, just taller
5 mm or 6 mm low-iron glass
bestFor: Jungle or forest-style layouts, tall stem plants and hardscape that breaks the surface.
watchOut: Height costs light at the substrate, so pair the taller models with a stronger fixture or low-light plants at the bottom.

name: Rimless Long Aquarium
summary: Long, narrow tanks that trade depth for a panoramic view. They give schooling nano fish a good run of open water and suit layouts that flow from one end to the other.
highlights: Four sizes: 45L, 60L, 90B and 90L (about 13 L to 81 L)
Narrow depth keeps them shelf and sideboard friendly
Good swimming length for tetras and rasboras
5 mm to 8 mm glass
bestFor: Sideboard or shelf setups and river-style layouts built for a shoal of small fish.
watchOut: The shallow depth makes it harder to create a sense of perspective, so plan the layout carefully.

name: Limited Edition Rimless Aquarium
summary: Four popular UNS sizes with a frosted blue back panel and a heat-fused white bottom. The dimensions and build match the standard tanks; the difference is a built-in backdrop that makes plants and fish stand out without adding a separate background.
highlights: Available as 5N, 45U, 60U and 90L
Satin frosted blue background panel
White fused bottom panel
Same glass thickness and sizes as the regular UNS range
bestFor: Someone who wants a clean backdrop without fitting a film or light panel behind the tank.
watchOut: The backdrop is permanent, and the white base will show through anywhere the substrate is thin.

name: Prism Glass Tank with Flush Lid
summary: Tall rimless cubes that come with a mitred glass lid sitting flush with the top. The lid has a vent hole and grips, and it cuts evaporation and keeps jumpy fish in.
highlights: Three sizes: 20TM, 25TM and 30TM (about 12 L to 37 L)
Flush-fitting glass lid with a central vent hole included
Tall proportions for vertical planting
5 mm glass with a stabilising foam mat included
bestFor: Small cube aquariums where you want a lid that disappears, such as a betta, shrimp or specimen-plant nano.
watchOut: The lid traps heat and moisture, so keep an eye on condensation and temperature under a strong light.

specs.Lid: Flush mitred glass lid with vent hole and grips

name: All-In-One Aquarium 30A
summary: A 30 cm rimless cube with a filter chamber built into the back behind a white panel. It hides the pump and media, so you avoid a canister and external pipes on a small tank.
highlights: 30 x 30 x 30 cm with about 21 L of display water
Rear filter chamber holds about 5.7 L
White background panel hides the equipment
Outflow nozzle included; pump and media are separate
bestFor: A tidy desktop nano where you do not want tubing or a canister on show.
watchOut: The pump is not included (UNS suggests the Sigma 5), and the chamber leaves less room for media than a canister would.

name: 90-Degree Rimless Aquarium
summary: The budget side of the UNS range: rimless tanks with plain 90 degree joins instead of mitred corners. The glass is clear and the sizes cover common cube, nano and 45 to 60 cm footprints for noticeably less money.
highlights: Cube, nano and standard sizes from 16 cm to 60 cm
Butt-joined 90 degree corners rather than mitred edges
5 mm glass (6 mm on the 60 cm tanks)
Levelling mat included
bestFor: A first planted tank or a shrimp and betta setup where cost matters more than seamless corners.
watchOut: The glass edges are visible at the corners, which some people notice once the tank is scaped.

name: Foresta Integrated Paludarium
summary: A complete paludarium in one glass box: a waterfall back wall covered in fibre mats, a hidden rear filter chamber with a pump, and an ultrasonic mister for the fog effect. You can grow mosses and rhizome plants on the wall and aquatic plants in the pool below.
highlights: Four sizes: 35E, 60E, 75E and 90E
Waterfall wall keeps the plant mats wet for mosses, ferns and Bucephalandra
Rear chamber with USB pump and bio sponges included
One Atomizer mister on the 35E and 60E, two on the 75E and 90E
6 mm glass on the smaller two, 8 mm on the larger two
bestFor: Anyone who wants a living moss wall or a land-and-water display without building the plumbing themselves.
watchOut: Constant misting and flowing water need regular top-ups and cleaning, and the rear chamber eats into display depth.

specs.Included: Pump, bio sponges, Atomizer mist maker, plant pad mats, Foresta LINE thread, chamber lid, foam mat

name: Paludarium Tank
summary: A rimless tank with a tall back and a low front, so you get a pool of water at the front and room for land and emersed plants behind it. Two 20 mm holes in the back panel take UNS bulkheads, letting a Delta canister run the water section.
highlights: Three sizes: 5E, 45E and 60E (about 8 L to 26 L of water)
Stepped glass: tall back panel, low front panel
Two pre-drilled 20 mm holes for bulkhead fittings
Also sold as an Enclosure Kit with two glass lids, clips and bulkheads to raise humidity
bestFor: Wabi-kusa and riparian layouts where you want to plumb in a canister filter and a mister.
watchOut: It is an open build; you need to add your own filter, mister and light, and the enclosure lids are not airtight.

specs.Options: Tank only, tank with bulkhead set, or Enclosure Kit with lids and clips

extra.Bulkhead holes: 2 x 20 mm in the back panel
2 x 20 mm in the back panel
2 x 20 mm in the back panel

name: Atomizer Mister Set
summary: A small ultrasonic fogger that sits just under the water and sends a low layer of mist across the surface. It raises humidity for emersed plants and looks good doing it.
highlights: Compact unit, about 5 x 4 x 4 cm
Needs at least 1.3 cm of water above it and cuts out if the level drops
Comes with a splash guard and three spare diffusion plates
Included with every Foresta paludarium
bestFor: Open shallow tanks and paludariums with emersed growth that likes humid air.
watchOut: Diffusion plates wear and scale up over time, and hard water makes that happen faster.

specs.Included: Mist maker, power plug, 3 diffusion plates, plate key, splash guard

name: Nimbus
summary: A programmable misting system with its own reservoir, pump and nozzles. You set the interval, duration and frequency, and it sprays a fine mist through up to five nozzles to keep enclosed plants from drying out.
highlights: About 12 L reservoir
Four spray nozzles supplied, supports up to five
Programmable interval, duration and frequency
Comes with 10 m of tubing, connectors and a tube cutter
bestFor: Enclosed paludariums and terrariums where plants need regular misting while you are away.
watchOut: Nozzle clips are sold separately, and fine nozzles clog with hard water, so use RO or distilled water.

specs.Included: Nimbus unit, 2 x 10 m tubing, 4 nozzles, connectors, plugs, clamps, tube cutter, power supply

name: Aquarium Tank Stand
summary: Pre-assembled wooden cabinets sized to match UNS tanks exactly, from the 30C cube up to the 180U. Each has a soft-close door and cut-outs in the sides and back for hoses and cables, with room inside for a canister filter and other equipment.
highlights: Sixteen sizes matched to UNS cube, U, P and L tanks
All stand 80 cm tall
Arrives fully assembled
Four finishes: Oak, Natural Wood Grain, Jet Black and Piano White
Side and rear openings for filter tubing and cables
bestFor: A UNS tank owner who wants a stand that matches the footprint to the centimetre.
watchOut: The finish is water resistant, not waterproof, so wipe up drips and spills promptly.

specs.Finishes: Oak, Natural Wood Grain, Jet Black, Piano White

name: Aluminium Aquarium Stand
summary: An aluminium cabinet for the larger UNS tanks, borrowed from the brand's reef systems. There are no steel hinges to rust; the doors are magnetic and lift off completely, which makes working on a filter or CO2 setup inside much easier.
highlights: Seven sizes from 60C to 180U
Fully removable magnetic doors (3 to 5 depending on size)
Levelling feet included
Grey or white finish
83 cm tall
bestFor: Large planted tanks where rust-free construction and full access to the cabinet matter.
watchOut: It needs assembling, and it costs noticeably more than the wooden stands.

specs.Included: Levelling feet, anti-scratch bumper pads, assembly hardware

name: Delta Canister Filter
summary: A compact white canister range that covers everything from a 5N nano to a 120 cm tank. Version 2 ships with Aquario Neo Flow lily pipes and media, it self-primes, and the baskets lift out separately for cleaning.
highlights: Four sizes: Delta 30, 60, 90 and 120
Rated for tanks up to about 61 L, 102 L, 250 L and 348 L
Low power draw: 7 W to 24 W
Aquario Neo Flow inflow and outflow pipes included (V2)
Neo Flow add-ons (skimmer, CO2 mixer, gentle outlet) fit straight on
bestFor: Nano to mid-size planted tanks where you want a small, tidy canister with clear lily pipes out of the box.
watchOut: Real flow at working height is roughly half the headline figure, so size up if you run CO2 in a densely planted tank.

specs.Included: Aquario Neo Flow lily pipes, filter media (V2)

name: Blitz Stainless Steel Filter
summary: A tiny canister filter with a brushed stainless steel body and matching steel pipes. It is made for nano tanks where a plastic canister would look out of place, and it runs quietly on low wattage.
highlights: Two sizes: 6 oz (tanks up to about 10 L) and 32 oz (up to about 45 L)
Stainless steel canister with matching inflow and outflow pipes
6 oz runs from USB; 32 oz uses a 12 V supply
Only 2 W and 5 W
bestFor: Nano and desktop tanks where the filter sits on show next to the aquarium.
watchOut: Media capacity is small, especially on the 6 oz, so expect to clean it more often than a bigger canister.

specs.Included: Canister, steel inflow and outflow pipes, clear tubing, power cable, tool, foam mat

name: Sigma Water Pump
summary: Small submersible DC pumps with an adjustable flow dial. They are the return pumps UNS pairs with its all-in-one tanks, and they also work as a general-purpose pump in a sump or DIY build.
highlights: Four sizes from about 300 L/h to 1,500 L/h
Flow is adjustable on the pump
Low-voltage DC (5 V on the Sigma 5, 12 V on the others)
IPX8 fully submersible
bestFor: Powering the rear chamber of an all-in-one tank, or a small custom filter or sump.
watchOut: Pick the size to match your tank's chamber; the listed flow drops quickly as head height goes up.

name: Delta Mini Surface Skimmer
summary: A small stand-alone skimmer that pulls oily film and floating debris off the surface. The outlet sits below the waterline, so it clears the surface without splashing away the CO2 you are paying for.
highlights: Up to about 250 L/h, adjustable
Only 3.5 W
Suits tanks of roughly 30 to 180 L
Works as a tiny extra filter as well as a skimmer
bestFor: CO2-injected planted tanks that keep getting a protein film on the surface.
watchOut: It is white and sits in the tank, so it is visible in a minimal layout.

name: Micro Aquarium Heater
summary: A very small heater for pico and nano tanks, with the thermostat and display on an external controller on the cable. The heating element is tiny enough to hide behind a rock, and it switches itself off if the water drops too low.
highlights: 10 W for about 4 to 8 L, 20 W for about 8 to 19 L
External digital controller on the cable
Low-water auto shut-off
10 W runs from USB; 20 W uses a mains plug
bestFor: Betta tanks and nano cubes under 20 litres where a normal glass heater would dominate the tank.
watchOut: The 20 W version has a US mains plug and 110 V rating, so check it suits your country's supply.

specs.Safety: Auto shut-off when water level is low

name: Titan 1 RGB LED
summary: A 90 W hanging LED with 200 RGB diodes in a wide aluminium body. One unit covers a 60 to 90 cm tank, and the wide spread keeps the light even across the footprint rather than hot in the middle.
highlights: 90 W with 200 RGB LEDs
One unit covers a 60 to 90 cm tank; use two or more for bigger tanks
About 300 PAR directly under the light at 30 cm
Exposed heat-sink fins to shed heat
Brushed black or silver aluminium
bestFor: Mid-size high-tech planted tanks where you want a pendant hung above an open-top rimless tank.
watchOut: It is designed to hang at least 30 cm above the water; the ceiling or hanging kit is sold separately.

specs.Mounting: Suspension wires (97 cm) included; hanging kit sold separately

extra.Recommended hanging height: 30 cm or more above the tank

name: Micro CO2 Kit
summary: The smallest complete pressurised CO2 setup UNS makes. It pairs the Micro regulator, solenoid and bubble counter with a 95 g disposable cartridge on a stand, so a nano tank can run on a timer without a big cylinder in sight.
highlights: Micro regulator, Micro solenoid and bubble counter included
Runs on 95 g disposable CO2 cartridges
Cartridge stand, tubing and diffuser included
Small enough to sit beside a desktop tank
bestFor: Nano and desktop planted tanks where you want timed, pressurised CO2 on a small budget.
watchOut: Disposable cartridges cost more per gram than a refillable cylinder, so it gets expensive on bigger tanks.

specs.Included: Regulator, solenoid, bubble counter, cartridge, stand, tubing, diffuser

name: Nano CO2 Kit
summary: A cartridge-based kit built around the Mini Dual Stage regulator. You get the stability of a dual-stage regulator with a built-in solenoid, but in a size that fits beside a small tank.
highlights: Mini Dual Stage regulator with built-in solenoid
95 g disposable cartridge on a stand
Tubing and diffuser included
Regulator can later move to a paintball or full-size cylinder
bestFor: Tanks of roughly 4 to 40 litres where you want dual-stage stability without a large cylinder.
watchOut: A cartridge lasts around two to three months on a small tank, so running costs add up compared with refilling.

specs.Included: Regulator, cartridge, stand, CO2 tubing, diffuser

name: Paintball CO2 Kit
summary: The Mini Dual Stage regulator paired with a refillable paintball cylinder. It holds a lot more gas than a cartridge but still fits in a small cabinet, which makes it a sensible middle step.
highlights: Mini Dual Stage regulator with built-in solenoid
16 oz or 24 oz refillable paintball cylinder
Cylinder has its own on/off valve
Tubing and diffuser included
bestFor: Small to medium planted tanks where cartridges run out too fast but a full-size cylinder will not fit.
watchOut: The cylinder ships empty, so you need a local refill source before you can start.

name: Pro CO2 Kit
summary: A full-size refillable CO2 system: a UNS Pro cylinder with the Pro Dual Stage regulator (the 2.5 lb kit uses the Mini regulator). It is the long-term option, with fewer refills and room to split gas across several tanks.
highlights: Cylinder sizes: 2.5, 5, 10 or 20 lb
Pro Dual Stage regulator with two gauges and bubble counter manifolds
Standard CGA-320 fittings, refillable at gas and welding suppliers
Tubing and diffuser included
bestFor: Medium to large high-tech tanks, or several tanks fed from one cylinder.
watchOut: Cylinders ship empty and need hydrostatic testing every five years in many regions.

specs.Regulator: UNS Pro CO2 Dual Stage (Mini Dual Stage on the 2.5 lb kit)

name: Micro CO2 Regulator
summary: A pocket-sized aluminium regulator that screws onto UNS disposable cartridges. On its own it is a manual regulator; add the Micro solenoid and bubble counter (sold together as the Regulator Kit) to put it on a timer.
highlights: Tiny gunmetal aluminium body
Made for UNS 95 g disposable cartridges
Modular: add the Micro solenoid and bubble counter
Also sold as a Regulator Kit with solenoid and bubble counter
bestFor: Desktop nanos where every centimetre of space around the tank counts.
watchOut: It only takes disposable cartridges, so you cannot move it to a refillable cylinder later.

extra.Includes: Micro regulator, Micro solenoid, Micro bubble counter

name: Micro CO2 Solenoid
summary: The add-on solenoid for the Micro regulator. Plug it into a timer and your CO2 switches on and off with the lights instead of running all night.
highlights: Fits the UNS Micro CO2 Regulator
Allows timer-controlled CO2
Compact block that keeps the Micro setup small
bestFor: Anyone already running the Micro regulator who wants CO2 on a schedule.
watchOut: It only fits the Micro regulator; the Mini and Pro regulators already have a solenoid built in.

name: Micro CO2 Bubble Counter
summary: A small detachable bubble counter with a check valve built in. It lets you see and set your bubble rate while stopping water from running back into the regulator.
highlights: Built-in check valve
Fits the UNS Micro, Mini and Pro regulators
Clear body for easy bubble counting
bestFor: Fine-tuning bubble rate on any UNS regulator, or as a spare.

specs.Compatible with: UNS Micro, Mini Dual Stage and Pro Dual Stage regulators

name: Mini CO2 Dual Stage Regulator
summary: A compact dual-stage regulator with a built-in solenoid that works with three gas sources out of the box: disposable cartridges, paintball cylinders and full-size CGA-320 cylinders. It grows with you if you move to a bigger tank.
highlights: Dual stage, so no end-of-tank dump as the cylinder empties
Built-in solenoid with power adapter
CGA-320 adapter fitted, paintball adapter included
Bubble counter included
bestFor: Nano and small tanks, especially if you might switch from cartridges to a refillable cylinder later.
watchOut: It has a single gauge, so you get less warning of an empty cylinder than with the Pro's two gauges.

specs.Cylinder: CGA-320, paintball (adapter included) and UNS disposable cartridges
specs.Included: CGA-320 adapter, paintball adapter, bubble counter, power adapter, spare o-rings, tools

name: Pro CO2 Dual Stage Regulator
summary: A full-size dual-stage regulator with two gauges, a built-in solenoid and two bubble counter manifolds. Add more manifolds and one cylinder can feed several tanks.
highlights: Dual stage with working and cylinder pressure gauges
Built-in solenoid
Two bubble counter manifolds included, expandable to about eight outputs
For CGA-320 cylinders from 2.5 to 20 lb
Anodised space grey finish
bestFor: Medium to large planted tanks and fish rooms running refillable cylinders.
watchOut: It is bulky and only takes CGA-320 cylinders, so it is overkill for a single nano.

specs.Included: CGA-320 adapter, 2 bubble counter manifolds, power adapter, spare o-rings, tools

name: CO2 Cylinder Pro
summary: Refillable aluminium CO2 cylinders with standard CGA-320 valves, from a cabinet-friendly 2.5 lb up to 20 lb. Bigger cylinders mean fewer trips to the refill station.
highlights: Four sizes: 2.5, 5, 10 and 20 lb
DOT 3AL certified aluminium
Standard CGA-320 valve for Pro and Mini regulators
White finish with UNS branding
bestFor: Anyone running a Pro or Mini regulator who wants the lowest running cost per fill.
watchOut: Ships empty, and must be hydrostatically tested every five years before it can be refilled in the US.

name: CO2 Paintball Cylinder
summary: Small refillable aluminium cylinders that sit between disposable cartridges and full-size bottles. The built-in on/off valve makes swapping them safer than a pin-valve paintball tank.
highlights: 16 oz or 24 oz capacity
Integrated on/off valve
Pairs with the UNS Mini Dual Stage regulator
About 22 cm and 28 cm tall
bestFor: Small to medium tanks where a full-size cylinder will not fit in the cabinet.
watchOut: Needs a paintball adapter on the regulator (one comes with the Mini Dual Stage).

name: CO2 Diffuser
summary: A clear acrylic in-tank diffuser with a white ceramic disc that breaks CO2 into a fine mist of bubbles. Acrylic makes it harder to break than the usual glass diffusers.
highlights: Three sizes by tank volume: Small, Medium, Large
Ceramic disc diameters of 12, 17 and 24 mm
Transparent acrylic, less fragile than glass
Suction cup included
bestFor: Any pressurised CO2 tank where you want a simple, low-cost in-tank diffuser.
watchOut: Discs clog over time and need a soak in diluted bleach to restore fine bubbles.

name: Pro Inline CO2 Diffuser
summary: An inline diffuser that fits in your canister's outflow hose, so CO2 is dissolved before the water reaches the tank and nothing extra sits in the scape. The ceramic disc is side-mounted, which keeps flow restriction down and makes it easy to swap.
highlights: Three hose sizes: 12/16, 16/22 and 20/25 mm
Side-mounted replaceable ceramic disc
Keeps diffuser clutter out of the tank
12 mm fits Delta 60/90 and Blitz 32 oz; 16 mm fits Delta 120
bestFor: Canister-filtered CO2 tanks where you want a clean, equipment-free look inside the glass.
watchOut: It needs a canister with enough flow, and the disc will need cleaning or replacing now and then.

name: Drop Checker
summary: A drop checker that changes colour with the CO2 level in your tank, giving you an at-a-glance check that injection is in the right range. It comes in a hang-on style for rimless tanks and a suction-cup style for anything else.
highlights: HD hangs over rimless glass up to 10 mm thick
SD fixes inside the tank with a suction cup
15 ml indicator solution included
30 ml refills sold separately
bestFor: Anyone running pressurised CO2 who wants a simple visual check.
watchOut: Drop checkers lag the tank by an hour or two, so read them late in the photoperiod.

extra.Fits: Rimless tanks with glass up to 10 mm

name: Aquascaping Scissors
summary: Stainless steel aquascaping scissors in the four shapes most planted tanks need: straight for stems, curved for shaping, wave for carpets and short spring scissors for nano detail work.
highlights: Straight, curved and wave at 25 cm long
Straight and curved spring scissors at 15 cm
Rust-resistant stainless steel
Black or grey finish on the long scissors
bestFor: Anyone putting together a basic trimming kit for a planted tank.
watchOut: Dry them after use; even stainless tools will spot if left wet.

name: Aquascaping Tweezers
summary: 25 cm stainless steel planting tweezers in straight and curved versions. Straight is the all-rounder for stems and general work; curved reaches in behind rocks and wood.
highlights: Straight and curved tips
25 cm long
Rust-resistant stainless steel
Black or grey finish
bestFor: Planting stems, tucking in epiphytes and general tidying in small to mid-size tanks.
watchOut: At 25 cm they are short for deep tanks over about 45 cm tall.

name: Pro Aquascaping Scissors
summary: The upgraded UNS scissors, with a stabilising tail on the handle so your hand has more support during long trimming sessions. Available as straight scissors for stems and wave scissors for carpets.
highlights: Straight and wave blades
25 cm long
Stabilising tail grip for comfort and control
Black or grey satin finish
bestFor: Regular trimmers with dense stem or carpet layouts who spend a while at the tank each week.
watchOut: Only two blade shapes in the Pro line, so you may still want a curved pair from the standard range.

name: Pro Aquascaping Tweezers
summary: Straight planting tweezers with a wider body for grip and slim, lightly serrated tips. They hold fine-rooted carpet plants firmly without crushing them.
highlights: Straight tips, 25 cm long
Wider body for better control
Light serration grips without tearing
Black or grey satin finish
bestFor: Planting carpets and fine-rooted plants where precision matters.

name: Sand Flattener
summary: A double-ended stainless steel spatula for levelling and shaping substrate. Use the wide end to smooth a foreground and the narrow end for tight spots around rocks.
highlights: Dual-ended: wide and narrow heads
25 cm long
Works with sand, gravel and aquasoil
Stainless steel
bestFor: Neat sand foregrounds, slopes and tidying soil between hardscape.

name: Algae Scraper
summary: A 30 cm stainless steel scraper with a replaceable razor blade for getting algae and film off the glass. Two blades come in the box.
highlights: 30 cm reach
Replaceable blades, two included
Stainless steel handle
bestFor: Keeping the front glass of a rimless tank clear of spot algae.
watchOut: Razor blades will scratch acrylic, so use it on glass only and keep sand grains out from under the blade.
